whatItDoes: Crops images with a draggable rectangle and 8 resize handles. Supports aspect presets (Free, 1:1, 4:3, 16:9, 9:16, 3:2, 2:3) with ratio locking, live dimmed overlay outside the crop, and export to JPEG/PNG/WebP at chosen quality. Works entirely in the browser via canvas.
whyItExists: Cropping for thumbnails, profile pictures, and social posts requires precise aspect control and visual feedback. Server uploads risk privacy and are slow; this tool gives pixel-accurate cropping locally with tiled handles and keyboard nudging without ever uploading the image.
whoShouldUse: Designers preparing social assets, developers generating thumbnails, and anyone needing quick, private image cropping without Photoshop or cloud converters.
useCases: Crop a photo to 1:1 for an Instagram profile picture with exact centering
Crop a 16:9 banner from a larger photo for a YouTube thumbnail
Use Free mode to cut out a specific object from a screenshot
Nudge the crop 1px with arrow keys for pixel-perfect alignment before export
Export the same crop as JPEG (90), PNG, and WebP to compare file sizes
instructions: Click or drop a JPEG/PNG/WebP image (10MB max). A centered 70% crop appears.
Pick an aspect preset (Free, 1:1, 4:3, etc.) — ratio locks and recenters the rectangle.
Drag the rectangle to move, or drag any of the 8 handles to resize. Shift+arrow nudges 10px, arrow nudges 1px, Enter crops.
Choose output format (JPEG/PNG/WebP) and quality (for JPEG/WebP).
Click Crop to generate the preview, then Download (or Download as PNG/WebP). The cropped image never leaves your browser.
examples: Input: 3000×2000 photo, preset 1:1, crop 1400×1400 centered → Output: 1400×1400 JPEG, ~300KB at 90 quality.
Input: 1920×1080 screenshot, Free mode, crop 800×600 around a dialog → Output: 800×600 PNG with sharp text preserved.
bestPractices: Use Free for arbitrary cuts, locked ratios for social presets to avoid distortion
For WebP, compare quality 85 vs 90 via preview file size before downloading
Reset crop if you switch aspect — it recenters to avoid empty edges
commonMistakes: Dragging outside the image — the clamp prevents negative coordinates but watch the dimmed overlay
Expecting EXIF to carry over — cropping creates a new bitmap without original metadata
Using very small MIN_CROP (20px) then upscaling — keep crops above 200px for quality
faq: Is the image uploaded? No — cropping uses canvas in your browser. Files never leave your device.
What aspect ratios are supported? Free, 1:1, 4:3, 16:9, 9:16, 3:2, 2:3. Free allows any rectangle; locked ratios resize proportionally.
Can I nudge with keyboard? Yes — focus the crop area, arrow keys move 1px, Shift+arrow moves 10px, Enter crops.
Does it preserve quality? Yes — the output is rendered at the crop's pixel size via drawImage, no upscaling unless you resize handles beyond the source.
features: Draggable rectangle with 8 handles and dimmed outside
Aspect presets with ratio locking and keyboard nudging
Export to JPEG/PNG/WebP with quality control
